objects.description: Calendar/time breakdown structure used by time utilities in this header. Represents local date and time components.
Thread-safe byte FIFO buffer with blocking read and bounded capacity FIFO_BUFFER_LEN. Provides read/write methods; platform-specific constructor initializes synchronization primitives.
Axis-aligned rectangle utility with integer coordinates, width/height helpers, containment tests, and equality comparison.
Bitmap description for 16-bit (RGB565) images used by image drawing. Holds dimensions, bit depth, and pointer to pixel data array (RGB565).
Glyph lattice entry for a single UTF-8 code point: pixel width and RLE-like pixel buffer used by lattice font renderer.
Font descriptor for lattice fonts: fixed height, number of glyphs, and array of LATTICE entries sorted by utf8_code for binary search.
Global theme registry providing static maps for fonts, images, and colors indexed by enums. Used by widgets for styling.
Z-order levels for layered drawing on a surface; MAX is a sentinel upper bound.
Optional external driver interface for display rendering when not writing directly to a framebuffer.
Display abstraction managing a physical framebuffer or external driver. Allocates and manages multiple GUI surfaces, flushes, draws primitives, and performs slide swipe animation between surfaces.
Internal layer record used by c_surface to represent a z-order layer's framebuffer, bounds, and currently active sub-rectangle.
Off-screen surface with optional layered framebuffers for z-order rendering. Can draw primitives per layer, manage active overlay rectangles, and flush changes to a c_display.
Abstract font renderer interface providing text and numeric drawing onto c_surface with alignment and size measurement utilities.
Concrete lattice font renderer implementing c_font_operator. Renders UTF-8 strings using LATTICE_FONT_INFO glyphs with simple alpha blending over background.
Static facade for text rendering that delegates to a global c_font_operator implementation (default c_lattice_font_op).
Abstract image renderer interface. Implementations draw full or partial images with an optional mask color for transparency.
Bitmap renderer for BITMAP_INFO images. Supports mask color handling and compositing with lower z-order layer content where mask matches.
Static facade for image rendering delegating to a global c_image_operator (default c_bitmap_operator).
Bitmask flags for widget/window attributes: visibility, focusable, and priority input handling.
Widget state machine values used for painting and interaction.
Logical navigation keys for non-touch input: forward/backward focus and enter/activate.
Touch action types delivered to widgets.
Declarative window tree node used to build child widget hierarchies with positions and captions.

objects.definition: typedef void (c_wnd::*WND_CALLBACK)(int, int);
objects.description: Pointer-to-member-function type for callbacks on c_wnd instances taking (id, param).
Base window/widget class providing hierarchy management, painting, input handling (touch/navigation), and common properties like rect, z-order, and theme/font.
Clickable button widget with pressed/focused visuals and callback invocation on release.
Mapping entry relating an active dialog to its associated surface, used internally by c_dialog static registry.
Dialog window with layer activation/deactivation support and static tracking per surface; supports modal priority behavior.
Soft keyboard capitalization state.
Soft keyboard layout style: full alphanumeric or numeric board.
Keyboard click result codes sent to owner callbacks.
On-screen keyboard widget that can be opened by an editor; manages key state, emits callbacks, and draws its own UI on a higher z-order layer.
Specialized button for keyboard keys with custom labels per key code and visuals tied to keyboard caps state.
Editable text widget integrating with c_keyboard for on-screen entry, maintaining input buffer and committed text with navigation handling.
Simple label widget that draws text with optional background color, left/vertical-center aligned.
Dropdown-like list box that expands on push to show selectable items on a higher z-order layer and notifies selection changes.
Container managing up to MAX_PAGES child slides displayed on separate surfaces; supports gesture-driven horizontal swipe transitions.
State machine for gesture handling: moving vs idle.
Gesture helper for c_slide_group to track horizontal swipe motion and drive real-time move and final page transitions.
Arrow button used by c_spin_box to increment/decrement value; forwards clicks to owning spin box.
Numeric spinner control displaying a value and hosting two arrow buttons to change it; notifies changes via callback.
Grid/table widget capable of configuring rows/columns, cell sizes, and drawing string items with alignment.
Circular buffer for waveform samples with utilities to read per-frame min/max/mid values for rendering and caching across refreshes.
Wave draw mode enumeration (currently not used in drawing logic in this header).
Waveform visualization control that renders streaming sample data from c_wave_buffer with a moving cursor and saved background for erasing.

functions.name: register_debug_function
functions.signature: void register_debug_function(void (*my_assert)(const char* file, int line), void (*my_log_out)(const char* log));
functions.description: Registers user-provided callbacks for assert handling and logging used by the library. Call early during program initialization so subsequent asserts/logs route to these callbacks.
requirements: my_assert may be NULL; if NULL, platform fallback behavior is used.
my_log_out may be NULL; if NULL, platform fallback behavior is used.
Should be called before other logging/asserting functions for full effect.

functions.name: _assert
functions.description: Library-internal assert trigger. Emits to registered assert callback (if any) or to platform default. Use macro ASSERT(condition) to invoke.
requirements: file must be a valid C-string path (typically provided by __FILE__).
line should be the source line (typically provided by __LINE__).
Not intended for direct external use; prefer ASSERT macro.

functions.name: log_out
functions.description: Outputs a log string to the registered log callback or platform console/debug output if none registered.
requirements: log must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
May be called from multiple threads; platform implementations use standard I/O functions.

functions.name: get_time_in_second
functions.description: Returns current time in seconds from the system clock (platform dependent).

functions.name: second_to_day
functions.description: Converts an epoch-like seconds value to a T_TIME breakdown (year, month, day, hour, minute, second).
requirements: second should be a valid time value for the platform (typically Unix epoch seconds).

functions.name: get_time
functions.description: Returns the current local time as a T_TIME struct.

functions.name: start_real_timer
functions.description: Starts a periodic real-time callback running at REAL_TIME_TASK_CYCLE_MS intervals. The callback is invoked from a worker thread receiving timer events.
requirements: func must be non-NULL; otherwise the function returns without starting the timer.
Callback func will be invoked with arg = NULL.
On supported platforms, spawns helper threads; do not assume callback runs on the main thread.
Callback must be reentrant/thread-safe and return quickly to avoid backlog.

functions.name: register_timer
functions.signature: void register_timer(int milli_second, void func(void* param), void* param);
functions.description: Registers a periodic timer that invokes func(param) roughly every milli_second milliseconds using an internal timer thread.
requirements: milli_second > 0; otherwise the registration fails.
func must be non-NULL.
Timer granularity is TIMER_UNIT (50ms); actual period is milli_second / TIMER_UNIT ticks.

functions.name: get_cur_thread_id
functions.description: Returns the current thread identifier as an unsigned integer (platform dependent representation).

functions.name: create_thread
functions.signature: void create_thread(unsigned long* thread_id, void* attr, void *(*start_routine) (void *), void* arg);
functions.description: Creates a new thread that begins execution at start_routine(arg). Returns the created thread ID via thread_id when supported.
requirements: start_routine must be non-NULL.
thread_id must be a valid pointer if the caller expects the created ID to be returned.
attr is platform-specific and may be NULL to use defaults.
start_routine must have C signature void* (*)(void*).

functions.name: thread_sleep
functions.description: Sleeps the calling thread for the specified number of milliseconds.
requirements: milli_seconds is the sleep duration in milliseconds; platform minimum granularity applies.

functions.name: build_bmp
functions.signature: int build_bmp(const char *filename, unsigned int width, unsigned int height, unsigned char *data);
functions.description: Writes a 16-bit RGB565 framebuffer (width×height) to a BMP file at filename. Returns 0 on success, -1 on file open error (and 0 for unsupported platforms).
requirements: filename must point to a writable path.
width and height must be > 0.
data must point to a buffer of size width*height*2 bytes encoded as RGB565.
On little-endian platforms the function writes in bottom-up scanline order.

functions.name: c_fifo::c_fifo
functions.description: Constructs a fixed-size FIFO (ring buffer) with platform-specific synchronization primitives for blocking reads and thread-safe writes.
requirements: No caller parameters. Buffer size is FIFO_BUFFER_LEN bytes (1024).

functions.name: c_fifo::read
functions.description: Reads exactly len bytes from the FIFO into buf, blocking until enough data is available. Returns the number of bytes read (len) or 0/<len only on platform-specific error paths.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len >= 0; len > 0 to actually read.
May block until data becomes available.
Thread-safe with internal synchronization.

functions.name: c_fifo::write
functions.description: Attempts to write len bytes from buf into the FIFO. If the buffer would overflow, logs a warning, discards the partial write, and returns 0. Returns len on success.
requirements: buf must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
len >= 0; len > 0 to actually write.
Notifies waiting readers when data is written.
Thread-safe with internal synchronization.

functions.name: c_theme::add_font
functions.signature: static int c_theme::add_font(FONT_LIST index, const void* font);
functions.description: Registers a font resource pointer at the given FONT_LIST index for later retrieval.
requirements: index must be < FONT_MAX; otherwise the function ASSERTs internally and returns -1.
font can be NULL if the caller intends to clear/leave empty, but later get_font(index) will return NULL.

functions.name: c_theme::get_font
functions.description: Retrieves the font pointer previously registered at index.
requirements: index must be < FONT_MAX; otherwise ASSERTs and returns 0.
Return value may be NULL if no font was set for index.

functions.name: c_theme::add_image
functions.signature: static int c_theme::add_image(IMAGE_LIST index, const void* image_info);
functions.description: Registers an image resource pointer (e.g., BITMAP_INFO) at the given IMAGE_LIST index.
requirements: index must be < IMAGE_MAX; otherwise ASSERTs and returns -1.
image_info may be NULL if the caller intends to clear/leave empty.

functions.name: c_theme::get_image
functions.description: Retrieves the image pointer previously registered at index.
requirements: index must be < IMAGE_MAX; otherwise ASSERTs and returns 0.
Return value may be NULL if no image was set for index.

functions.name: c_theme::add_color
functions.signature: static int c_theme::add_color(COLOR_LIST index, const unsigned int color);
functions.description: Registers a color value at the given COLOR_LIST index.
requirements: index must be < COLOR_MAX; otherwise ASSERTs and returns -1.

functions.name: c_theme::get_color
functions.signature: static const unsigned int c_theme::get_color(COLOR_LIST index);
functions.description: Retrieves the color value registered at index.
requirements: index must be < COLOR_MAX; otherwise ASSERTs and returns 0 (as a default).

functions.name: c_display::c_display
functions.signature: inline c_display::c_display(void* phy_fb, int display_width, int display_height, c_surface* surface, DISPLAY_DRIVER* driver = 0);
functions.description: Constructs a display bound to a single pre-created surface. The display uses the given physical framebuffer and optional external DISPLAY_DRIVER for drawing.
requirements: surface must be non-NULL and already configured with a color depth matching the framebuffer.
display_width > 0 and display_height > 0.
If driver is provided and its callbacks are non-NULL, they may override pixel/rect drawing.
phy_fb may be NULL if using an external DISPLAY_DRIVER for rendering.

functions.name: c_display::c_display
functions.signature: inline c_display::c_display(void* phy_fb, int display_width, int display_height, int surface_width, int surface_height, unsigned int color_bytes, int surface_cnt, DISPLAY_DRIVER* driver = 0);
functions.description: Constructs a display that manages multiple internal surfaces of the given size, color depth, and count.
requirements: color_bytes must be 2 or 4; otherwise ASSERTs.
surface_cnt <= SURFACE_CNT_MAX.
display_width > 0, display_height > 0; surface_width > 0, surface_height > 0.
Allocates surface_cnt c_surface instances; caller should manage lifetime of c_display.

functions.name: c_display::alloc_surface
functions.signature: inline c_surface* c_display::alloc_surface(Z_ORDER_LEVEL max_zorder, c_rect layer_rect = c_rect());
functions.description: Initializes the next available surface with the given maximum z-order and optional layer rectangle, and returns it. Used for slide groups or additional layers.
requirements: max_zorder < Z_ORDER_LEVEL_MAX; otherwise ASSERTs.
Must not exceed m_surface_cnt; otherwise ASSERTs.
If layer_rect is empty (default), it expands to the full display size.

functions.name: c_display::swipe_surface
functions.signature: inline int c_display::swipe_surface(c_surface* s0, c_surface* s1, int x0, int x1, int y0, int y1, int offset);
functions.description: Performs a horizontal swipe composition between two surfaces over a rectangle, moving content by offset pixels to create a slide transition. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: s0 and s1 must be non-NULL and share the same c_display if using driver draw path in certain branches.
0 <= offset <= s0->m_width.
x0..x1 and y0..y1 must be within the surfaces’ bounds; function clamps to display bounds but ASSERTs on invalid ranges.
Updates internal write index; intended to be called during gestures/animations.

functions.name: c_display::get_width
functions.description: Returns display width in pixels.

functions.name: c_display::get_height
functions.description: Returns display height in pixels.

functions.name: c_display::get_phy_fb
functions.description: Returns the pointer to the physical framebuffer used by the display, or NULL if rendering via external driver only.

functions.name: c_display::get_updated_fb
functions.signature: void* c_display::get_updated_fb(int* width, int* height, bool force_update = false);
functions.description: Returns the framebuffer pointer if there has been an update since the last read (tracked by internal indices). If force_update is true, always returns the framebuffer. Optionally outputs width/height.
requirements: If width and height pointers are non-NULL, they will be set to display dimensions.
If no updates and not forced, returns NULL.
Only meaningful when a physical framebuffer is used (non-NULL).

functions.name: c_display::snap_shot
functions.description: Saves the current framebuffer to a BMP file. Supports 16-bit or 32-bit internal color bytes. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure or unsupported configuration.
requirements: file_name must be a valid path to create a file.
m_phy_fb must be non-NULL.
m_color_bytes must be 2 or 4; for 32-bit, the data is converted to RGB565 before writing.

functions.name: c_surface::get_max_z_order
functions.description: Returns the maximum z-order level configured for this surface.

functions.name: c_surface::c_surface
functions.signature: c_surface::c_surface(unsigned int width, unsigned int height, unsigned int color_bytes, Z_ORDER_LEVEL max_zorder = Z_ORDER_LEVEL_0, c_rect overlpa_rect = c_rect());
functions.description: Constructs a surface with given size and color depth. Optionally sets up layer storage for z-order-based rendering, using either full size or an overlap rectangle.
requirements: width > 0, height > 0.
color_bytes is typically 2 or 4 to match the display.
If overlpa_rect is empty, the entire surface area is used.
Allocations for layer framebuffers occur based on max_zorder and display context.

functions.name: c_surface::get_pixel
functions.signature: unsigned int c_surface::get_pixel(int x, int y, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Returns the 32-bit ARGB-like color at (x,y) from the specified z-order or fallback backing buffers. Converts from 16-bit buffers when necessary.
requirements: 0 <= x < m_width and 0 <= y < m_height; otherwise ASSERTs and returns 0.
z_order < Z_ORDER_LEVEL_MAX.
A valid source buffer must be present in the layer, surface, or display; otherwise returns 0.

functions.name: c_surface::draw_pixel
functions.signature: virtual void c_surface::draw_pixel(int x, int y, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Draws a pixel at (x,y) with provided 32-bit RGB on the given z-order, considering layer overlap and active rectangles. Updates display when active.
requirements: Coordinates must be within surface bounds; out-of-range calls are ignored.
z_order <= m_max_zorder; otherwise ASSERTs and returns.
For off-top layers, the layer rect must contain the point to be drawn into that layer.
Display must be attached for on-screen update when active.

functions.name: c_surface::fill_rect
functions.signature: virtual void c_surface::fill_rect(int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Fills a rectangle with a solid color at the specified z-order, honoring layering and overlap. For top or max layers may optimize to low-level fill.
requirements: Coordinates are corrected/clamped within surface bounds internally.
z_order should be <= m_max_zorder.
Layer framebuffer must exist for non-top layers to receive pixels.

functions.name: c_surface::fill_rect
functions.signature: void c_surface::fill_rect(c_rect rect, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Overload to fill a rectangle defined by a c_rect at the given z-order.
requirements: rect must be initialized (width>0, height>0).

functions.name: c_surface::draw_hline
functions.signature: void c_surface::draw_hline(int x0, int x1, int y, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Draws a horizontal line from x0 to x1 at y using draw_pixel semantics for the given z-order.
requirements: x0 <= x1 for any visible output.
y within [0, m_height).

functions.name: c_surface::draw_vline
functions.signature: void c_surface::draw_vline(int x, int y0, int y1, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Draws a vertical line from y0 to y1 at x using draw_pixel semantics for the given z-order.
requirements: y0 <= y1 for any visible output.
x within [0, m_width).

functions.name: c_surface::draw_line
functions.signature: void c_surface::draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Draws a line between (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) using an integer Bresenham-like algorithm via draw_pixel at the given z-order.
requirements: Coordinates ideally within surface bounds; out-of-range pixels are ignored by draw_pixel.

functions.name: c_surface::draw_rect
functions.signature: void c_surface::draw_rect(int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int z_order, unsigned int size = 1);
functions.description: Draws a rectangle frame with the specified border thickness (size) at the given z-order.
requirements: size >= 1 for visible output.
Coordinates may be in any order; lines are drawn via draw_hline/draw_vline.

functions.name: c_surface::draw_rect
functions.signature: void c_surface::draw_rect(c_rect rect, unsigned int rgb, unsigned int size, unsigned int z_order);
functions.description: Overload to draw a rectangle border defined by a c_rect.
requirements: rect must be initialized (width>0, height>0).

functions.name: c_surface::flush_screen
functions.signature: int c_surface::flush_screen(int left, int top, int right, int bottom);
functions.description: Copies a rectangular region from the surface framebuffer to the display framebuffer and notifies the display of an update. Returns 0 on success, -1 if not active.
requirements: Surface must be active; otherwise returns -1.
left/right/top/bottom must be within surface bounds; ASSERTs on invalid parameters.
Display and surface framebuffers must be set up.

functions.name: c_surface::is_active
functions.description: Returns whether the surface is actively driving the display (updates mirrored to display).

functions.name: c_surface::get_display
functions.description: Returns the display attached to this surface, or NULL if none attached.

functions.name: c_surface::activate_layer
functions.signature: void c_surface::activate_layer(c_rect active_rect, unsigned int active_z_order);
functions.description: Sets the active rectangle for a given z-order layer, revealing lower layers in the previously active region when deactivating/changing regions.
requirements: active_z_order must be > Z_ORDER_LEVEL_0 and <= Z_ORDER_LEVEL_MAX; otherwise ASSERTs.
active_rect may be empty to inactivate the layer.

functions.name: c_surface::set_active
functions.description: Enables or disables on-screen mirroring of subsequent surface drawing operations.

functions.name: c_font_operator::draw_string
functions.signature: virtual void c_font_operator::draw_string(c_surface* surface, int z_order, const void* string, int x, int y, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color) = 0;
functions.description: Interface: draw a null-terminated string at coordinates using the specified font and colors.
requirements: surface must be non-NULL.
string must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated string for the active font implementation.
font must be a valid font object for the implementation or NULL if supported by implementation.
z_order must be valid for the surface.

functions.name: c_font_operator::draw_string_in_rect
functions.signature: virtual void c_font_operator::draw_string_in_rect(c_surface* surface, int z_order, const void* string, c_rect rect, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color, unsigned int align_type = ALIGN_LEFT) = 0;
functions.description: Interface: draw a string within a rectangle with alignment, using the specified font and colors.
requirements: surface and string must be non-NULL.
rect must be valid (width>0,height>0).

functions.name: c_font_operator::draw_value
functions.signature: virtual void c_font_operator::draw_value(c_surface* surface, int z_order, int value, int dot_position, int x, int y, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color) = 0;
functions.description: Interface: draw a numeric value at coordinates with a decimal dot position formatting.
requirements: dot_position is expected 0..3 by the lattice implementation.

functions.name: c_font_operator::draw_value_in_rect
functions.signature: virtual void c_font_operator::draw_value_in_rect(c_surface* surface, int z_order, int value, int dot_position, c_rect rect, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color, unsigned int align_type = ALIGN_LEFT) = 0;
functions.description: Interface: draw a numeric value within a rectangle with alignment and dot formatting.
requirements: rect must be valid.
dot_position range depends on implementation (0..3 for lattice).

functions.name: c_font_operator::get_str_size
functions.signature: virtual int c_font_operator::get_str_size(const void* string, const void* font, int& width, int& height) = 0;
functions.description: Interface: measure a string’s rendered width and height for the given font. Returns 0 on success, negative on failure.
requirements: string and font must be valid for the implementation.

functions.name: c_lattice_font_op::draw_string
functions.signature: void c_lattice_font_op::draw_string(c_surface* surface, int z_order, const void* string, int x, int y, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color);
functions.description: Renders a UTF-8 string using a lattice font onto the surface at (x,y), blending font_color over bg_color per glyph pixel coverage.
requirements: string must be UTF-8 null-terminated.
font must point to a valid LATTICE_FONT_INFO; if NULL, an error glyph "X" is drawn.
surface and z_order must be valid.
Coordinates should be within drawing area for visible output.

functions.name: c_lattice_font_op::draw_string_in_rect
functions.signature: void c_lattice_font_op::draw_string_in_rect(c_surface* surface, int z_order, const void* string, c_rect rect, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color, unsigned int align_type = ALIGN_LEFT);
functions.description: Renders a UTF-8 string aligned within rect using the lattice font and colors.
requirements: rect must be valid; alignment must be a combination of ALIGN_* flags.
string and font as per draw_string.

functions.name: c_lattice_font_op::draw_value
functions.signature: void c_lattice_font_op::draw_value(c_surface* surface, int z_order, int value, int dot_position, int x, int y, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color);
functions.description: Formats an integer value with a decimal dot (0..3 places) and draws it at (x,y) using the lattice font.
requirements: dot_position must be 0,1,2, or 3; otherwise ASSERTs.
font must be a valid LATTICE_FONT_INFO.

functions.name: c_lattice_font_op::draw_value_in_rect
functions.signature: void c_lattice_font_op::draw_value_in_rect(c_surface* surface, int z_order, int value, int dot_position, c_rect rect, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color, unsigned int align_type = ALIGN_LEFT);
functions.description: Formats a value with a decimal dot and draws it aligned within rect using the lattice font.
requirements: rect must be valid; dot_position 0..3.
font must be valid.

functions.name: c_lattice_font_op::get_str_size
functions.signature: int c_lattice_font_op::get_str_size(const void* string, const void* font, int& width, int& height);
functions.description: Computes pixel width and height for a UTF-8 string using the lattice font. Returns 0 on success, -1 if string or font is NULL.
requirements: string must be UTF-8; font must be a valid LATTICE_FONT_INFO.

functions.name: c_word::draw_string
functions.signature: static void c_word::draw_string(c_surface* surface, int z_order, const void* string, int x, int y, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color);
functions.description: Static convenience wrapper that forwards to the configured font operator to draw a string.
requirements: fontOperator must be initialized (done by library when GUILITE_ON).
Parameters as per font operator.

functions.name: c_word::draw_string_in_rect
functions.signature: static void c_word::draw_string_in_rect(c_surface* surface, int z_order, const void* string, c_rect rect, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color, unsigned int align_type = ALIGN_LEFT);
functions.description: Wrapper that draws a string within a rect with alignment via the configured font operator.
requirements: Parameters as per font operator; rect must be valid.

functions.name: c_word::draw_value_in_rect
functions.signature: static void c_word::draw_value_in_rect(c_surface* surface, int z_order, int value, int dot_position, c_rect rect, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color, unsigned int align_type = ALIGN_LEFT);
functions.description: Wrapper that draws a formatted value in a rectangle via the configured font operator.
requirements: dot_position semantics per font operator.
rect must be valid.

functions.name: c_word::draw_value
functions.signature: static void c_word::draw_value(c_surface* surface, int z_order, int value, int dot_position, int x, int y, const void* font, unsigned int font_color, unsigned int bg_color);
functions.description: Wrapper that draws a formatted value at coordinates via the configured font operator.
requirements: dot_position semantics per font operator.

functions.name: c_word::get_str_size
functions.signature: static int c_word::get_str_size(const void* string, const void* font, int& width, int& height);
functions.description: Wrapper that measures a string via the configured font operator. Returns 0 on success, negative on failure.
requirements: string and font must be valid for the configured font operator.

functions.name: c_image_operator::draw_image
functions.signature: virtual void c_image_operator::draw_image(c_surface* surface, int z_order, const void* image_info, int x, int y, unsigned int mask_rgb = DEFAULT_MASK_COLOR) = 0;
functions.description: Interface: draw an image at (x,y) using optional mask color for transparency.

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: text string (C-style, UTF-8/ASCII), delivered via FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# Goals for interesting inputs across provided stubs:
# - Non-empty printable ASCII words
# - Short strings to satisfy tight widget limits (e.g., edit<32, list item<=16, unit<=8, name<=16)
# - Mixed whitespace, punctuation, and alignment markers
# - UTF-8 multibyte sequences (valid)
# - Numeric-looking strings
# - Edge cases: single char, very short, length near typical limits
# - Repeated characters and mask-like sequences
#
# The fuzzer runtime will request a single input buffer per execution and may slice it for
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() or treat the entire buffer as the initial corpus. We therefore return a
# bytes blob containing multiple newline-separated candidate strings so the harness can split
# or sample from them. Each line is a valid UTF-8 sequence without embedded NUL; C++ side
# uses std::string which supplies a terminating NUL via c_str().
#
# Size cap: keep under 4096 bytes.

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

# Some valid UTF-8 multibyte examples
UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    " café",               # Latin-1 supplement
    "—dash—",              # em dash
    "測試文本",             # CJK
    "π≈3.14159",           # Greek/pi
    "🙂 emoji",            # emoji (4-byte UTF-8)
    "Γειά σου",           # Greek
]

KEYWORDS = [
    "A", "OK", "Yes", "No", "NULL", "true", "false",
    "Title", "Label", "Item", "Value", "Name", "Unit",
    "0123456789", "-123", "+456", "3.1415", "1,234", "0xDEADBEEF",
    "left", "center", "right", "align", "mask", "transparent",
]

# Length-bounded generators for different API constraints

def gen_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(L)).strip() or "A"

def gen_numeric_like(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    choices = ["0", "1", "-1", "+1", "12345", "-32768", "32767", "3.14", "0.000", "99999"]
    s = rng.choice(choices)
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s

def gen_utf8(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    s = rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES)
    if len(s) > max_len:
        # attempt to trim at codepoint boundaries (Python slices are codepoint-safe)
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s

def bounded(rng: random.Random, s: str, max_len: int, min_fallback: str = "A") -> str:
    s = s[:max_len]
    if not s:
        s = min_fallback
    return s

def unique_pad(rng: random.Random, s: str, target_len: int) -> str:
    if len(s) >= target_len:
        return s[:target_len]
    pad_char = rng.choice([" ", ".", "_", "-"])
    return s + pad_char * (target_len - len(s))

# Compose a palette of strings tailored to the stubs

def build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # General log/message strings (varied)
    out.append("Hello, world!")
    out.append("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.")
    out.append("The quick brown fox jumps over 13 lazy dogs.")
    out.append(rng.choice(KEYWORDS))
    out.append(gen_ascii(rng, 3, 24))

    # Font drawing: include UTF-8, punctuation, and whitespace
    out.append("Text")
    out.append(" align:left ")
    out.append("[UI] Render @ z=1")
    out.append(gen_utf8(rng, 24))
    out.append("mix: äöüß ñ ñandú")

    # Tight limits for various widgets
    # c_edit::set_text requires < 32
    out.append(bounded(rng, gen_ascii(rng, 5, 30), 30))
    out.append(bounded(rng, gen_utf8(rng, 30), 30))

    # c_list_box::add_item <= 16
    out.append(bounded(rng, "Item-" + gen_ascii(rng, 1, 10), 16))
    out.append(bounded(rng, gen_numeric_like(rng, 16), 16))

    # c_wave_ctrl labels: name<=16, unit<=8
    out.append(bounded(rng, "Wave", 16))
    out.append(bounded(rng, "mV", 8))

    # c_table::set_item typical cell content <= 16
    out.append(bounded(rng, "Cell", 16))
    out.append(bounded(rng, "R1C1", 16))

    # Very short and single-char cases
    out.append("A")
    out.append("0")
    out.append(" ")

    # Numeric-looking and hex strings
    out.append("1234567890")
    out.append("-42")
    out.append("0xBEEF")

    # Alignment hint strings (though align is numeric param, text still varied)
    out.append("centered text")
    out.append("right>>")

    # Mask-like color text
    out.append("MASK=0xF81F")

    # Some repeated chars
    out.append(unique_pad(rng, "----", rng.randint(4, 12)))
    out.append(unique_pad(rng, "====", rng.randint(4, 12)))

    # More UTF-8 with emoji; keep short
    out.append(bounded(rng, "🙂", 8))

    # Ensure non-empty distincts and trim to safe sizes
    final: List[str] = []
    for s in out:
        s = s.replace("\n", " ")  # keep line-structured corpus clean
        if not s:
            s = "A"
        # hard cap any individual line to 64 bytes to stay small overall
        s = s[:64]
        final.append(s)

    # Add a few random short ascii lines for extra coverage
    for _ in range(6):
        final.append(bounded(rng, gen_ascii(rng, 1, rng.randint(4, 20)), 32))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    dedup: List[str] = []
    for s in final:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            dedup.append(s)

    return dedup


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    lines = build_strings(rng)
    # Join with newlines so the harness can split; no embedded NULs
    data = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    b = data.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        # ensure we end on a newline to avoid truncating a UTF-8 codepoint mid-line
        if not b.endswith(b"\n"):
            # try to backtrack to last newline boundary
            nl = b.rfind(b"\n")
            if nl != -1:
                b = b[:nl + 1]
    return b

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: raw binary file data
# Used by fuzz stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME as a writable output target.
# For build_bmp and c_display::snap_shot, the filename is opened for writing.
# The contents we return here will be pre-existing file bytes, but these
# functions only write to the file (overwrite). However, some harnesses may
# pre-create the file with our bytes or check initial contents. We'll generate
# plausible BMP-like headers of varying sizes to exercise file handling paths
# while remaining valid generic binary data.

MAX_BYTES = 4096


def _rand(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def _make_minimal_bmp(rng: random.Random, w: int, h: int, bpp: int = 16) -> bytes:
    # Create a minimal BMP file with BITMAPFILEHEADER + BITMAPINFOHEADER and pixel data.
    # BMP stores rows bottom-up, padded to 4-byte boundaries.
    # bpp=16 to align with RGB565 used by the library. We'll pick BI_BITFIELDS (3) mask case sometimes.
    use_bitfields = (bpp == 16) and (rng.random() < 0.5)

    # Headers
    bfType = b"BM"  # 0x4D42
    # BITMAPINFOHEADER (40 bytes)
    biSize = 40
    biWidth = w
    biHeight = h
    biPlanes = 1
    biBitCount = bpp
    biCompression = 3 if use_bitfields else 0  # BI_BITFIELDS or BI_RGB
    # Compute row size (padded to 4 bytes)
    row_bits = w * bpp
    row_bytes = ((row_bits + 31) // 32) * 4
    image_size = row_bytes * h

    # Optional bit masks for 16bpp (RGB565)
    masks = b""
    if use_bitfields:
        # RGB565 masks
        red_mask = 0xF800
        green_mask = 0x07E0
        blue_mask = 0x001F
        masks = struct.pack("<III", red_mask, green_mask, blue_mask)

    biXPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biYPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biClrUsed = 0
    biClrImportant = 0

    bfOffBits = 14 + biSize + len(masks)
    bfSize = bfOffBits + image_size
    bfReserved1 = 0
    bfReserved2 = 0

    # Build headers
    file_header = struct.pack(
        "<2sIHHI",
        bfType,
        bfSize,
        bfReserved1,
        bfReserved2,
        bfOffBits,
    )
    info_header = struct.pack(
        "<IIIHHIIIIII",
        biSize,
        biWidth,
        biHeight,
        biPlanes,
        biBitCount,
        biCompression,
        image_size,
        biXPelsPerMeter,
        biYPelsPerMeter,
        biClrUsed,
        biClrImportant,
    )

    # Pixel data: simple gradient/pattern
    pixels = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        # bottom-up rows: content doesn't matter for validity here
        row = bytearray()
        if bpp == 16:
            for x in range(w):
                # Build an RGB565 pattern varying with x and y
                r = (x * 31) // max(1, (w - 1))
                g = (y * 63) // max(1, (h - 1))
                b = ((x + y) * 31) // max(1, (w + h - 2))
                rgb565 = ((r & 0x1F) << 11) | ((g & 0x3F) << 5) | (b & 0x1F)
                row += struct.pack("<H", rgb565)
        else:
            # 24 bpp fallback (unlikely used), write blue-green-red
            for x in range(w):
                r = (x * 255) // max(1, (w - 1))
                g = (y * 255) // max(1, (h - 1))
                b = ((x + y) * 255) // max(1, (w + h - 2))
                row += bytes((b, g, r))
        # pad to 4-byte boundary
        while len(row) % 4 != 0:
            row += b"\x00"
        pixels += row

    bmp = file_header + info_header + masks + bytes(pixels)
    # Ensure we don't exceed MAX_BYTES; if too big, downscale
    if len(bmp) > MAX_BYTES:
        # Reduce height first
        scale = max(1, len(bmp) // MAX_BYTES + 1)
        new_h = max(1, h // scale)
        if new_h == h:
            new_h = max(1, h // 2)
        return _make_minimal_bmp(rng, w, new_h, bpp)
    return bmp


def _bmp_like_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose reasonable small dimensions to keep size well under 4KB
    w = _rand(rng, 1, 64)
    # Cap height such that pixel payload fits
    max_h = max(1, (MAX_BYTES // 4) // w)
    h = _rand(rng, 1, min(128, max_h))
    return _make_minimal_bmp(rng, w, h, 16)


def _pattern_blob(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate a structured binary blob with multiple sections to vary IO paths
    sections: List[bytes] = []
    # Header magic and version
    sections.append(b"GFXF\x00\x01")
    # Add a few TLV-like entries
    remaining = size - sum(len(s) for s in sections)
    while remaining > 4:
        t = rng.choice([b"TIME", b"IMAG", b"TEXT", b"DATA"])  # 4 bytes
        # pick payload length up to 64 bytes
        plen = min(remaining - 6, _rand(rng, 0, 64))
        if plen < 0:
            break
        entry = t + struct.pack("<H", plen)
        payload: bytes
        if t == b"TIME" and plen >= 8:
            # pack a plausible T_TIME-like breakdown in ASCII for readability
            y = _rand(rng, 1970, 2099)
            mo = _rand(rng, 1, 12)
            d = _rand(rng, 1, 28)
            hh = _rand(rng, 0, 23)
            mm = _rand(rng, 0, 59)
            ss = _rand(rng, 0, 59)
            payload = f"{y:04d}-{mo:02d}-{d:02d} {hh:02d}:{mm:02d}:{ss:02d}".encode()
            payload = payload[:plen].ljust(plen, b"\x00")
        elif t == b"IMAG" and plen >= 16:
            # embed a tiny fake RGB565 row
            pixels = bytearray()
            for _ in range(plen // 2):
                pixels += struct.pack("<H", rng.randrange(0, 0x10000))
            if len(pixels) < plen:
                pixels += b"\x00"
            payload = bytes(pixels[:plen])
        elif t == b"TEXT":
            s = rng.choice([
                "Hello",
                "GuiLite",
                "Slide/Swipe",
                "WaveCtrl",
                "Bitmap565",
                "ThemeMap",
            ])
            payload = s.encode()[:plen].ljust(plen, b" ")
        else:
            payload = rng.randbytes(plen)
        sections.append(entry + payload)
        remaining = size - sum(len(s) for s in sections)
    blob = b"".join(sections)
    return blob[:size]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose among several valid, interesting binary layouts. These are not fuzz-mutations
    # but structured binaries that can exist on disk harmlessly and potentially affect
    # path coverage in file I/O code that might peek or rely on sizes.
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.55:
        # Produce a minimal valid BMP file (16bpp), small size
        data = _bmp_like_blob(rng)
    elif choice < 0.8:
        # Produce a generic structured blob of moderate size
        size = _rand(rng, 64, min(1024, MAX_BYTES))
        data = _pattern_blob(rng, size)
    else:
        # Raw deterministic pattern bytes of bounded size
        size = _rand(rng, 1, min(2048, MAX_BYTES))
        # Repeating 0xAA/0x55 patterns used by the stub's initial buffer
        pat = [0xAA, 0x55, 0x00, 0xFF]
        buf = bytearray(size)
        for i in range(size):
            buf[i] = pat[(i + rng.randrange(0, 4)) % len(pat)]
        data = bytes(buf)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_BYTES]
    return data
